rationale: Recurring noun on this page (lines 1, 23, 30) denoting cosmic conflict. Pairs with ⲧⲃⲉⲟ̄ⲥⲉ 'depth' and is the subject of cosmogonic 'arise' (ϣⲱⲡⲉ). Etymology uncertain — possibly Lyc form related to a martial root or to ⲕⲣⲱϥ 'guile'; the contextual semantics demand a conflict-noun.

ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲣ̄- ('do/make') + ⲡⲁⲓⲥ (uncertain root). Since ⲡⲁⲇⲁⲙⲁⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'Adamas of Light' is the cosmic warrior figure who battles the abortions/dragons, 'place of battle' fits the discourse. ⲡⲁⲓⲥ may be a Lyc form for combat/striking.
Lyc reflex of ⲗⲱⲕϩ̄ 'cast, throw, immerse.' Intransitive in line 12: 'they sank into the three earths' until the Third Ambassador's revelation.

Qualitative/perfect verb describing the state of paths after the Ambassador's revelation. Context demands a path-opening or path-extending sense. Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲱϣⲧ̄ 'lift up' or ⲥⲱⲕ-class verb.

Line 20: 'the X of the ⲡⲕⲙ̄ⲧⲟ which arose in the watch of the Pherrokatochos.' Etymology unclear. Possibly related to ⲕⲙⲟⲙ 'be black' (giving 'darkness') or to ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲙⲧⲟ 'before, in presence of' (giving 'occasion'). Confidence low.

Greek-derived cosmological title (φερρόκατοχος < φέρω + κατέχω 'bear and hold-down'), associated with the Pillar of Glory in the Manichaean cosmic-bearing schema. Distinct from the Omophoros (line 16) and the Pillar of Glory itself, which 'comes forth' in this watch.
Modifier of ⲡⲕⲣⲁϩ 'strife' in line 23. Likely Lyc qualitative of ϩⲁϣ 'many, much.'
Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'prison' (Crum). The 'prison of the dark ones' is the eschatological prison of the fallen Watchers in the Manichaean appropriation of 1 Enoch.

proposed_english: the watch / the period of duty
rationale: Recurring chapter-structuring term (lines 9, 16, 20, 24, 29): 'in the watch of [Power X].' Each cosmic Power has a 'watch' — a temporal-functional period during which their characteristic event unfolds. The kephalaion enumerates these in sequence. Likely Lyc reflex of ⲣⲟⲉⲓⲥ/ⲱⲣϣ 'watch, vigil.'

Greek ἐγρήγοροι 'Watchers' — the fallen Watchers of 1 Enoch tradition. Manichaean reception identifies them as the cosmic figures who descended from heaven, were bound by the four angels in the prison of darkness, and whose giant sons were expelled from earth.
Line 20 noun governed by 'the' and modifying ⲡⲕⲙ̄ⲧⲟ. Etymology unclear; possibly Lyc form of ⲗⲱⲓϫⲉ 'cause, occasion' or related to ⲗⲱⲟⲩ 'thing.'
